evidence.excerpt: A 120-hour fed-batch fermentation of Corynebacterium glutamicum ATCC 13032 for glutamic acid production was operated with deliberate dissolved oxygen (DO) setpoint transitions (30%, 50%, and 70% air saturation, each held for 40 hours) to examine the effect of oxygen availability on both productivity and mutation accumulation. Glutamic acid titre was highest at 50% DO (48.3 g/L versus 41.1 g/L at 30% and 43.7 g/L at 70%). Whole-genome sequencing of 96 single colonies harvested from each DO phase identified mutation frequencies of 3.1 × 10⁻⁴, 1.8 × 10⁻⁴, and 5.6 × 10⁻⁴ mutations per genome per generation at 30%, 50%, and 70% DO respectively, with oxidative stress response genes overrepresented among mutations at 70% DO. The results caution against high-DO operation strategies adopted for productivity reasons without parallel strain stability monitoring.
